folds.heading: ## Slack-map reconciliation: measured tradeoffs and geometry limits (B248, 2026-11-04)
folds.body:
F1. Full numeric review covers all324 data rows across six R16/R18/R20 before/after slack tables: nine fresh/populated/combat cases at1366×768/14,1366×768/21 and1920×1080/21, each with player/focus/inventory/actions/log/other rows. These are dated measurement artifacts, not freshly exercised builds or screenshots. Same page bounds can coexist with substantial internal module overflow; low region slack does not mean readable content, and large sparse-log slack does not prove another pane can grow without a task tradeoff. A module list may include nested/companion content, so its heights are not automatically additive independent regions.

F2. R16's populated1366/21 comparison records more visible inventory rows5→6 and less inventory overflow679→600 despite frame311→291, alongside scene90→60 and navigation45→33 reductions. Character221px, Focus188px and action202px overflow remain afterward. The density improvement is scoped rather than a no-scroll/no-overflow proof. Records/Skills also carry their own overflow in populated contexts. AD36/AD43 do not let a table of geometric changes replace the actual relevant task/keyboard/return/browser check.

F3. R18 tabs have a measurable cost that the short technical-close wording alone could hide: at1366/21 tools31→60px, populated belongings254→226px, rows6→5 and overflow600→641; combat rows5→4.1920 populated rows15→14 and overflow332→345. Retain category/search/clear/known-value benefits from their actual consumer evidence while recording this tradeoff. Under AD32 the historical tabs/layout are scoped choices, not proof every added toolbar improves density or permission to silently shrink text.

F4. R20 combat redistributes space:1920/21 player/focus497→429px and inventory/actions491→559px, inventory rows13→15 and action-module height353→421px. Log width stays501px and slack862px in that case.1366/21 rows5→6 and action frame266→291px. Those tables do not by themselves prove opponent countability, click stability, native fact filtering or current layout parity. R20-before similarities to R18-before are not byte-identity evidence; preserve each candidate's actual input record. Current desktop/prose-first/optional-art direction and optional human review under AD42 qualify historical viewport gates. No runtime or visual acceptance was renewed by reading these maps.
